clause: §9.8 / §9.9 (unchanged Apply stays a no-op; edited field changes only its edge)
claim: The four #content-box-* inputs are type=number step=0.1. After a real fractional drag, a rounded value such as 594.64 fails step validation (stepMismatch), so a real click on #content-apply-object shows Chromium's 'Please enter a valid value…594.6 and 594.7' bubble and never submits. The unchanged-Apply no-op check therefore passes only because nothing runs. It would pass on the pre-fix build too, since 594.6435 is also a mismatch, so shot-debt2 case B proves nothing. A human who edits W and clicks Apply gets no write at all. The passthrough logic itself is correct: dispatching submit directly gives a no-op for an unchanged form, and W=120 changes only the right edge.
reproduction: node .quad/shared/p6/checks/review-debt2-renderer-probe.mjs under the lock (log .quad/scratch/debt2/review-renderer/probe5.out, probe1.out): direct3, Edit text, real CDP drag of Im1 by (3,7) px with Meta held → placement [74.295,594.6435,174.295,644.6435]; fields 74.3/594.64/100/50; content-box-y.validity = stepMismatch; real Apply click → revision 7→7 with the validation bubble (review-out/review-debt2-renderer-d-apply-unchanged.png); W=120 + real Apply click → no write.
fix: Set step="any" on #content-box-x/-y/-w/-h (index.html:410,411,414,415). In shot-debt2.mjs B, assert content-object-form.checkValidity() before the Apply click so validation can no longer make the no-op pass.
